senses.definition: The pointing of a weapon, as a gun, a dart, or an arrow, or object, in the line of direction with the object intended to be struck; the line of fire; the direction of anything, such as a spear, a blow, a discourse, a remark, towards a particular point or object, with a view to strike or affect it.
examples: Take time with the aim of your gun.

2012, "The Legend of the Gobblewonker", season 1, episode 2 of Gravity Falls, spoken by Grunkle Stan, voiced by Alex Hirsch
My ex-wife still misses me, but her aim is getting better!

senses.definition: The point intended to be hit, or object intended to be attained or affected.

examples: My number one aim in life is to make money to make my parents, siblings, and kids happy.

senses.definition: The ability of someone to aim straight; one’s faculty for being able to hit a physical target.
examples: The police officer has excellent aim, always hitting the bullseye in shooting practice.
He has a bad aim, so he decided to join archery classes.

quotes.text: What you would work me to, I have some aim.

senses.definition: (intransitive) To point or direct a missile, or a weapon which propels as missile, towards an object or spot with the intent of hitting it
examples: He aimed at the target, but the arrow flew straight over it.

senses.definition: (intransitive) To direct the intention or purpose; to attempt the accomplishment of a purpose; to try to gain; to endeavor;—followed by at, or by an infinitive
examples: to aim to do well in life

quotes.text: The stories did not seem to me to touch life. They were plainly intended to have a bracing moral effect, and perhaps had this result for the people at whom they were aimed.

senses.definition: (transitive) To direct or point (e.g. a weapon), at a particular object; to direct, as a missile, an act, or a proceeding, at, to, or against an object
examples: to aim an arrow at the deer
She aimed a punch at her ex-boyfriend.
He aimed the gun at him and he held his hands up in surrender.

senses.definition: (transitive) To direct (something verbal) towards a certain person, thing, or group
examples: to aim a satirical comment at Communists in general

quotes.text: But, good my lord, do it so cunningly / That my discovery be not aimed at;
